summary: rustre-deobf-mhcde is a library crate (opaque-predicate / junk-code detection, MHCDE pipeline, multi-stage deobf) but has ZERO MCP tools registered in rustre-mcp-server. grep for 'mhcde|deobf_mhcde|opaque_predicate|junk_code' across crates/rustre-mcp-server/src returns no matches. The only deobf-family MCP tools are 'deobfuscate_strings' (rustre-analysis) and 'deobf_mba_normalize' (rustre-deobf-mba). Therefore no JSON-RPC comparison vs the Python validator is possible: the validator implements OpaquePredicateDetector/JunkCodeDetector/PatchPlanner equivalents but there is no corresponding MCP endpoint to invoke.
notes: Per workspace policy (feedback_warnings.md): the crate is uncabled functionality — proper follow-up is to wire it into rustre-mcp-server (e.g. expose tools like analysis_deobf_mhcde_scan / analysis_deobf_mhcde_patch_plan that wrap MhcdeOrchestrator::analyze). That is a feature task out of scope for this validation comparison.
Validator self-test still works standalone: detect_opaque_predicates + detect_junk_regions + build_patch_plan + analyze.
